case.task: We need to set up our new self-hosted CI runner by assigning specific custom operational labels to it in GitHub. Once that is done, please post a confirmation update directly into our #devops-deployments Slack channel so the team knows the runner is fully configured and ready for production builds.

candidate_tools.description: Adds and appends custom labels to a self-hosted repository runner, which must be registered and active.
Creates a new attachment and associates it with a specific, existing Linear issue.

(DEPRECATED: use `SLACK_SEND_MESSAGE`) Posts a message to a Slack channel, DM, or private group; requires at least one content field (`markdown_text`, `text`, `blocks`, or `attachments`) — omitting all causes a `no_text` error. Fails with `not_in_channel`, `channel_not_found`, or `channel_is_archived` if the bot lacks access. Body limit ~4000 characters. Rate-limited at ~1 req/sec (HTTP 429, honor `Retry-After`). Not idempotent — duplicate calls post duplicate messages.
Stars a channel, file, file comment, or a specific message in Slack.
Tool to check API calling code by testing connectivity and authentication to the Slack API. Use when you need to verify that API credentials are valid and the connection is working properly.

Grants an existing repository access to an existing organization-level Dependabot secret when the secret's visibility is set to 'selected'; the repository must belong to the organization, and the call succeeds without change if access already exists.

case.rationale: The workflow represents a realistic DevOps automation task where a GitHub self-hosted runner's labels are updated, followed by a status notification posted to a Slack channel.

arguments.query: We need to set up our new self-hosted CI runner by assigning specific custom operational labels to it in GitHub. Once that is done, please post a confirmation update directly into our #devops-deployments Slack channel so the team knows the runner is fully configured and ready for production builds.

toolkit_connection_statuses.status_message: No Active connection for toolkit=github. You MUST call COMPOSIO_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS (toolkit="github") to create a connection BEFORE executing any github tools.

GITHUB_SET_STATUS_CHECK_CONTEXTS.description: Replaces required status check contexts for a protected branch, requiring admin permissions; an empty `contexts` array removes all checks.

repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension; not case sensitive.

owner.description: The account owner (username or organization) of the repository; not case sensitive.

branch.description: The name of the branch for which to set status check contexts; cannot contain wildcard characters.

contexts.description: Names of the status checks to require; an empty array removes all required status checks.

MICROSOFT_TEAMS_TEAMS_POST_CHANNEL_MESSA.description: Posts a new top-level message to a channel in Microsoft Teams (does NOT reply to an existing message). Despite the file name 'reply_to_channel_chat', this action creates a brand-new message in the channel via POST /teams/{id}/channels/{id}/messages. To reply to an existing message thread, use the dedicated reply action instead.

locale.description: Locale of the channel message. Microsoft Teams currently documents this as client-set and always 'en-us'; only 'en-us' is supported.

content.description: The content of the message to be sent. Can be plain text or HTML, determined by `content_type`. To @mention someone, this must be HTML containing an <at id="0">Name</at> tag with a matching entry in `mentions`. To @mention a user, send content_type="html", wrap the name in an <at> tag, and add a matching mentions entry whose id equals the <at> id. For example: content_type="html", content='Hello <at id="0">Jane Smith</at>, please review.', mentions=[{"id": 0, "mentionText": "Jane Smith", "mentioned": {"user": {"id": "ef1c916a-3135-4417-ba27-8eb7bd084193", "displayName": "Jane Smith", "userIdentityType": "aadUser"}}}]. The mentioned user id must be the Microsoft Entra (Azure AD) object ID (a GUID), not an email or display name; resolve it first with a user-lookup action. Typing '@Name' into content does nothing: Graph still returns 201 but the name renders as plain text with no notification.

subject.description: The subject of the chat message, in plaintext. Optional field typically used for channel messages.

summary.description: Summary text for push notifications and summary views. Applies to channel chat messages.

team_id.description: The unique identifier of the Microsoft Teams team containing the channel.

id.description: Index of this mention. Must equal the id in the matching <at id="{id}"> tag in the message content. Number mentions from 0.
Microsoft Entra (Azure AD) object ID (GUID) of the mentioned user. Must be the directory object ID, not an email address or display name.

tenantId.description: Microsoft Entra tenant ID for the mentioned user. Optional for identities in the current tenant.

displayName.description: Display name of the mentioned user. Should match the text inside the corresponding <at> tag.

userIdentityType.description: Type of user identity. Use 'aadUser' for a normal member of the tenant.

id.description: ID of the mentioned application or bot.

tenantId.description: Microsoft Entra tenant ID for the mentioned application or bot.

displayName.description: Display name of the mentioned application or bot.

application.description: An application or bot @mentioned in a message.

id.description: ID of the mentioned conversation. Use the team ID for a team mention and the channel ID for a channel mention.

displayName.description: Display name of the mentioned team, channel, or chat.

conversation.description: A team, channel, or chat @mentioned in a message.

mentioned.description: The entity (user, conversation, or application) to @mention.

mentionText.description: Text representing the mention, such as the user's display name. Should match the text inside the matching <at> tag.

items.description: A single @mention to send with a message (Graph chatMessageMention).

mentions.description: Entities to @mention in the message. Each entry must pair with an <at> tag in `content` carrying the same id, and `content_type` must be 'html'. To @mention a user, send content_type="html", wrap the name in an <at> tag, and add a matching mentions entry whose id equals the <at> id. For example: content_type="html", content='Hello <at id="0">Jane Smith</at>, please review.', mentions=[{"id": 0, "mentionText": "Jane Smith", "mentioned": {"user": {"id": "ef1c916a-3135-4417-ba27-8eb7bd084193", "displayName": "Jane Smith", "userIdentityType": "aadUser"}}}]. The mentioned user id must be the Microsoft Entra (Azure AD) object ID (a GUID), not an email or display name; resolve it first with a user-lookup action. Typing '@Name' into content does nothing: Graph still returns 201 but the name renders as plain text with no notification.

channel_id.description: The unique identifier of the channel within the specified team where the message will be posted.

importance.description: The importance of the chat message. Possible values: 'normal', 'high', 'urgent'. Defaults to 'normal' if not specified.

attachments.description: References to attached objects like files, tabs, meetings, etc. Each attachment is a chatMessageAttachment object.

content_type.description: The format of the message content. Defaults to 'text'. Must be 'html' to @mention anyone; if `mentions` is provided this is automatically upgraded to 'html', since Graph only renders <at> tags in an HTML body.
Media type of the hosted content, such as image/png. Maps to contentType.

temporary_id.description: Temporary identifier used in message HTML or attachment content as ../hostedContents/{temporary_id}/$value. Maps to @microsoft.graph.temporaryId.

content_bytes.description: Base64-encoded bytes of the hosted content payload. Maps to contentBytes.

items.description: Hosted content to upload while posting a Microsoft Teams chat message.

hosted_contents.description: Hosted content objects to upload with the message. Reference each item from HTML or attachment content using ../hostedContents/{temporary_id}/$value.

GITHUB_CREATE_A_DEPLOYMENT.description: Creates a GitHub deployment for an existing repository, targeting a specific ref (branch, tag, or SHA) that must also exist within the repository.

ref.description: The ref to deploy. This can be a branch name, a tag name, or a commit SHA.

repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive. The repository must exist and the authenticated user must have write access to it.

task.description: Specifies a task to execute, e.g., `deploy` or `deploy:migrations`.

owner.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive. The repository must exist and the authenticated user must have access to it.

payload.description: A JSON string payload providing additional information that a deployment system might need, customizable based on the deployment process.

auto_merge.description: Attempts to automatically merge the default branch into the requested ref if the ref is behind the default branch. Set to `false` to disable.

examples: Deploying new feature X to staging.
description.description: A short description of the deployment. Maximum length of 1000 characters.

environment.description: Name for the target deployment environment (e.g., `production`, `staging`, `qa`).

required_contexts.description: A list of status check contexts to verify against commit status checks before creating the deployment. If omitted or `null`, GitHub verifies all unique contexts. Pass an empty list `[]` to bypass all checks.

transient_environment.description: Specifies if the given environment is specific to this deployment and will no longer exist at some point in the future (e.g., a staging environment for a pull request). Set to `true` if the environment is temporary.

production_environment.description: Specifies if the given environment is one that end-users directly interact with.

MICROSOFT_TEAMS_TEAMS_LIST_CHANNELS.description: Retrieves channels for a specified Microsoft Teams team ID (must be valid and for an existing team), with options to include shared channels, filter results, and select properties.

filter.description: OData v4 query string to filter channels (e.g., `startswith(displayName,'Sales')` or `membershipType eq 'private'`).

select.description: Comma-separated channel properties to return (e.g., 'id,displayName,description'); empty for default properties. Common: `id`, `displayName`, `description`, `email`, `membershipType`, `webUrl`.

team_id.description: Unique identifier (GUID/UUID) of the Microsoft Teams team. Must be in UUID format (e.g., '87b0560f-fc0d-4442-add8-b380ca926707'). Team names are not accepted. Use MICROSOFT_TEAMS_LIST_USER_JOINED_TEAMS to get team IDs.

page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit for the first page; then pass back the `next_page_token` from the previous response, unmodified, until it is absent. Do not construct or edit it. When set, it drives pagination; resend the same required identifier (team_id), but filter/select params need not be repeated — the token carries them.

include_shared_channels.description: If true, include channels shared with the team (uses allChannels endpoint). If false, exclude shared channels from results by filtering on membershipType.
